snippet.title: The First Man Frozen in Time!
snippet.description:
Meet James Bedford, the first man ever to be cryopreserved! On January 12, 1967, after passing away from kidney cancer, Bedford’s body was frozen with the hope that future science could one day bring him back to life. Using dry ice and liquid nitrogen, this pioneering process was groundbreaking, though primitive by today’s standards. While it's uncertain if he’ll ever be revived, Bedford’s story continues to inspire the human quest to overcome death. Every year, cryonics enthusiasts celebrate "Bedford Day" in his honor. PETA even sued on behalf of the monkey, Naruto, claiming he should hold the copyright! But in 2016, a U.S. court ruled that animals can’t own copyrights. The case was settled with 25% of future photo revenue going to charities protecting Naruto’s habitat. What do you think—was this fair, or just bananas?
